newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent pares earlier losses by late trading.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent pares earlier losses by late trading.

text.p: Brent crude futures pared earlier losses in late trading as bearish sentiment from Monday followed through to Tuesday, brokers said.
January Brent crude futures were last traded on SIMEX at $22.60 per barrel, down two cents from London's settlement on Monday but 10 cents above the SIMEX intraday low.
Brokers said the falls seen in both London and New York after news Iraq had agreed to all conditions in the oil-for-food deal, had prompted slightly bearish sentiment in Asia too.
January NYMEX crude, trading on the after-hours ACCESS system, was last traded at $23.43 per barrel, down six cents from New York. Earlier it had traded as low as $23.28.
On Monday, Iraq's U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon said Baghdad had agreed to all U.N. conditions to implement the $2 billion oil-for-food deal.
U.N. Secretary General Boutros Boutros-Ghali said he was optimistic for movement on the deal in a few weeks.
